'''Aday Mara Gómez''' (born April 7, 2005) is a Spanish [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]] and [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. Mara was an [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA national champion]] and the [[2025–26 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season#All-Big Ten awards and teams|Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year]] with Michigan in 2026. He previously played for [[Basket Zaragoza]].

==Early life==
Mara was born and raised in [[Zaragoza]], Spain. His father, Francisco Javier Mara, played basketball professionally for [[CB Zaragoza]] from 1986 to 1988.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2022/news/all-in-the-family-at-fiba-basketball-u17-world-cup-2022|title=All in the family at FIBA Basketball U17 World Cup 2022|website=FIBA.basketball|date=July 9, 2022|access-date=February 21, 2023}}</ref> His mother Angélica "Geli" Gómez, played volleyball on the [[Spain women's national volleyball team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heraldo.es/noticias/deportes/baloncesto/2022/10/28/aday-mara-y-lucas-langarita-pasan-a-ser-jugadores-de-la-primera-plantilla-del-casademont-zaragoza-1608797.html|title=Aday Mara y Lucas Langarita pasan a ser jugadores de la primera plantilla del Casademont Zaragoza|work=[[Heraldo de Aragón]]|date=October 28, 2022|access-date=February 21, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eldesmarque.com/zaragoza/basket-zaragoza/67821-aday-mara-y-lucas-langarita-cuando-el-exito-va-en-los-genes|website=El desmarque|title=Aday Mara y Lucas Langarita: cuando el éxito va en los genes|date=July 11, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.acb.com/jugador/temporada-a-temporada/id/20213226|website=[[Liga ACB|acb.com]]|title=Aday Mara|access-date=November 6, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/baloncesto/acb/2022/10/17/634cc46e46163fd7638b457b.html|website=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|date=October 17, 2022|title=Aday Mara, el unicornio español de 2,20 m., derriba la puerta con 17 años: debuta en la ACB haciendo historia|first=Enric|last=Corbella}}</ref> Mara's father and mother stand at {{convert|201|cm|ftin|order=flip}} and {{convert|190|cm|ftin|order=flip}}.<ref name="as" />

==Professional career==
After Mara began to play basketball for Básket Lupus, he joined Zaragoza Basket's youth categories.<ref name="bravo">{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldo.es/noticias/deportes/2021/11/23/baloncesto-casademont-zaragoza-aday-mara-cuando-el-limite-es-el-cielo-1535592.html|website=[[Heraldo de Aragón]]|title=Aday Mara, cuando el límite es el cielo|date=November 23, 2021|first=Chema M.|last=Bravo}}</ref> He was assigned in the lower tiers with Zaragoza's affiliated team Club Baloncesto El Olivar ([[EBA League]]).<ref name="elperiodicoaragon" /> He made his debut in [[LEB Oro]] in the also affiliated team [[CB Peñas Huesca|Levitec Huesca]] in a fixture against [[AB Castelló|Tau Castelló]] in October 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/baloncesto/basketfeb/2021/10/09/61614ee022601dba3b8b4635.html|website=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|date=October 9, 2021|title=Aday Mara, la torre de futuro del baloncesto español de 2,18 y 16 años, ilusiona en su brillante estreno en LEB Oro}}</ref> On November 17, 2021, Mara made his debut at age 16 with the first team of [[Casademont Zaragoza]] in a [[FIBA Europe Cup]] fixture against [[Pallacanestro Reggiana|Reggio Emilia]], scoring two points.<ref name="elperiodicoaragon">{{Cite web|url=https://www.elperiodicodearagon.com/cai-zaragoza/2021/11/17/casademont-zaragoza-reggio-emilia-directo-resultado-resumen-59642688.html|website=[[El Periódico de Aragón]]|title=Casademont Zaragoza-Reggio Emilia: El día que debutó Aday Mara|first=Raquel|last=Machín|date=November 17, 2021}}</ref> He played in the [[2020–21 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] and averaged 8.5 points, 10.5 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 3.5 [[block (basketball)|blocks]] over four games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/baloncesto/nba/20230221/1001945615/nba-alucina-aday-mara-all-star-limite-cielo.html|title=La NBA alucina con Aday Mara en el All Star: "Su límite es el cielo"|first=Toni|last=Canyameras|work=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|date=February 21, 2023|access-date=February 21, 2023|language=Spanish}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.20minutos.es/deportes/noticia/5100270/0/aday-mara-la-perla-del-baloncesto-espanol-a-la-conquista-de-la-nba/|title=Aday Mara, la perla del baloncesto español, a la conquista de la NBA|work=[[20 minutos]]|date=February 10, 2023|access-date=February 21, 2023|language=Spanish}}</ref>

Mara was loaned to [[CB Peñas Huesca]] of LEB Oro at the start of the 2021–2022 season due to a roster shortage at the club. He averaged 2.7 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 0.7 blocks over six games. Mara was then assigned to Anagan Olivar of [[Liga EBA]], the Spanish fourth division, where he averaged 10.8 points, 7.2 rebounds, 1.4 [[assist (basketball)|assists]], and 1.8 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2022/news/spain-big-man-mara-passing-his-way-to-star-prospect-status|title=Spain big man Mara passing his way to top prospect status|website=FIBA.basketball|date=July 3, 2022|access-date=February 21, 2023}}</ref> Mara made his [[Liga ACB]] debut with Zaragoza on October 16, 2022,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.relevo.com/baloncesto/liga-acb/aday-mara-gigante-espanol-asombra-20221017082452-nt.html|title=Aday Mara, el gigante español de 2,20 que asombra al mundo del baloncesto|first=Guillermo|last=García|website=[[Relevo]]|date=October 17, 2022|access-date=February 21, 2023|language=Spanish}}</ref><ref name="as">{{Cite web|url=https://as.com/baloncesto/aday-mara-el-unicornio-espanol-n/|website=[[AS (newspaper)|AS]]|date=November 6, 2022|first=José Ignacio|last=Pinilla|title=Aday Mara, el unicornio español}}</ref> chipping in eight points, four rebounds, one assist and one block.<ref>{{Cite web|website=[[Liga ACB|acb.com]]|date=October 16, 2022|title=Aday Mara, el gigante más joven de la historia de la Liga Endesa|url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/369434-aday-mara-el-gigante-mas-joven-de-la-historia-de-la-liga-endesa.html}}</ref> He also took part in the [[Basketball Without Borders]] camp during the [[2023 NBA All-Star Game|2023 NBA All-Star weekend]] in [[Salt Lake City, Utah]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/baloncesto/nba/la-nba-se-frota-las-manos-con-aday-mara-muchos-equipos-le-siguen-n/|title=La NBA se frota las manos con Aday Mara: "Muchos equipos le siguen"|work=[[Diario AS]]|date=February 21, 2023|access-date=February 21, 2023|language=Spanish}}</ref>

==College career==
===UCLA===
On August 3, 2023, the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA) announced Mara's signing to play [[college basketball]] in the United States for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 3, 2023 |title=UCLA Men's Basketball Signs Aday Mara |url=https://uclabruins.com/news/2023/8/3/ucla-mens-basketball-signs-aday-mara.aspx |access-date=August 14, 2023 |website=UCLA |language=en}}</ref> He was rated as a [[Blue chip (sports)|five-star recruit]] and the No. 15 overall prospect in the 2023 class by [[247Sports]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/player/aday-mara-46140859/high-school-294943/ |title=Aday Mara Recruiting Profile |website=[[247Sports]] |access-date=April 13, 2025}}</ref> Casademont Zaragoza contested his move, stating that "contracts must be respected" and warning that they would "take the necessary measures to keep it that way".<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 2, 2023 |title=Aday Mara, the Spanish giant that will play with UCLA in the NCAA |url=https://www.marca.com/en/ncaa/2023/08/02/64cad11722601d24428b45ad.html |access-date=August 14, 2023 |website=Marca |language=en}}</ref> The dispute led to potential [[NCAA]] eligibility issues for Mara, before he was cleared to play for UCLA three days before the start of the [[2023–24 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-10-27/ucla-aday-mara-berke-buyuktuncel-ncaa-eligiblity|title=UCLA still awaiting NCAA clearance on freshmen Aday Mara and Berke Buyuktuncel|first=Ben|last=Bolch|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=October 27, 2023|access-date=October 29, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=UCLA star freshman Aday Mara cleared by NCAA for competition|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/38810449/ucla-star-freshman-aday-mara-cleared-ncaa-competition|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=November 3, 2023|access-date=November 6, 2023}}</ref> He was a part-time [[starting lineup|starter]] during the season.<ref name=bolch_03312025>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=In a massive setback for UCLA, 7-3 center Aday Mara will not return next season|date=March 31, 2025|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2025-03-31/ucla-aday-mara-will-not-return|access-date=April 1, 2025}}</ref>

In [[2024–25 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2024–25]], Mara came almost entirely off the [[Substitution (sport)|bench]], but became a major part of the rotation after a breakout game against [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] in late January 2025.<ref name=bolch_03312025/> He scored a then-career-high 22 points in an 85–83 upset win over the No. 18 Badgers, halting their winning streak at seven. He shot seven-for-seven and added five rebounds, including four offensive, and had two blocks in a then-season-high 21 minutes.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Aday Mara makes his presence felt in UCLA's upset win over Wisconsin|date=January 21, 2025|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2025-01-21/ucla-mens-basketball-vs-wisconsin-recap|access-date=January 31, 2025}}</ref> Mara followed up with 12 points and seven rebounds along with then–career highs of 30 minutes and five blocks in a win over [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]]. His 51 minutes in two games bested his usage in the prior eight contests.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Aday Mara doesn't miss in crunch time as resurgent UCLA defeats Washington|date=January 24, 2025|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2025-01-24/resurgent-ucla-fends-off-washington-to-pick-up-its-third-consecutive-win|access-date=January 31, 2025}}</ref> In the following game against [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] with [[Tyler Bilodeau]] out injured, Mara made his only start of the season and recorded his first career [[double-double]] with  12 points and 11 rebounds along with five blocks again against [[UCLA–USC rivalry|UCLA's crosstown rivals]].<ref name=bolch_03312025/><ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Sebastian Mack's late heroics help UCLA edge USC and extend its winning streak|date=January 27, 2025|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2025-01-27/aday-mara-sebastian-mack-ucla-mens-basketball-usc|access-date=January 31, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Eric Dailey Jr., UCLA hang on for victory over USC|date=January 28, 2025|publisher=Reuters|agency=Field Level Media|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/eric-dailey-jr-ucla-hang-victory-over-usc-2025-01-28/|access-date=January 31, 2025}}</ref> In the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025 NCAA tournament]], he had 10 points, six rebounds, five blocks and two assists in 20 minutes in a  72–47 first-round win over [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA showcases its depth in dominant NCAA tournament win over Utah State|date=March 20, 2025|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2025-03-20/ucla-mens-basketball-vs-utah-state-aday-mara-march-madness|access-date=April 1, 2025}}</ref> He ended the season averaging 6.4 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.6 blocks in 13.1 minutes. Following his sophomore season, he entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]].<ref name=bolch_03312025/>

===Michigan===
On April 11, 2025, Mara transferred to the [[University of Michigan]] to play for head coach [[Dusty May]] and the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Wolverines]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2025/04/11/michigan-wolverines-basketball-adds-ucla-7-footer-aday-mara-from-transfer-portal/83045649007/ |title=Michigan basketball adds UCLA 7-footer Aday Mara from transfer portal |website=[[The Detroit News]] |first=James |last=Hawkins |date=April 11, 2025 |access-date=April 11, 2025}}</ref> On November 3 against [[2025–26 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|Oakland]], he had a double-double in his Michigan debut, recording twelve points, a career-high twelve rebounds, and tying a career-high with five blocks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2025/11/03/michigan-wolverines-basketball-oakland-golden-grizzlies-season-opener/87076278007/ |title=Michigan basketball shoots the lights out in 121-78 season-opening win over Oakland |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]] |first=Tony |last=Garcia |date=November 3, 2025 |access-date=November 9, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/aday-mara-2/gamelog/ |title=Aday Mara Career Game Log |website=[[Sports Reference]] |access-date=November 9, 2025}}</ref> On November 11 against [[2025–26 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]], Mara followed his impressive debut with a second double-double, recording 18 points, a career-high 13 rebounds, a career-high six assists, and again tied his career-high with five blocks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401817529 |title=Michigan v. Wake Forest |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 11, 2025 |access-date=November 11, 2025}}</ref> With these numbers, he became the second player in history to accumulate more than 30 points, 25 rebounds, 10 blocks and 5 assists in his first two games of a season in the [[NCAA Division I]] or [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], after [[Tim Duncan]] who did it in the [[2003–04 NBA season]] with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/baloncesto/2025/11/12/aday-mara-historia-baloncesto-norteamericano-igualando-tim-duncan.html |title=Aday Mara hace historia en el baloncesto norteamericano igualando a Tim Duncan |website=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |date=November 12, 2025 |access-date=November 12, 2025 |language=es}}</ref> On February 5, 2026, Mara posted a career-high six blocks in a 110–69 victory against [[2025–26 Penn State Nittany Lions basketball team|Penn State]], helping [[2025–26 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] to a school record 21st win before a second loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401825496|title=Burnett scores career-high 31, No. 2 Michigan routs Penn St 110-69 to reach school-record 21-1 mark|access-date=February 6, 2026|date=February 5, 2026|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> On February 8 in a [[Michigan–Ohio State men's basketball rivalry|rivalry game]] victory at [[2025–26 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]], Mara had a career-high 24 point effort that included his first two made collegiate [[three point shot]]s (after never attempting any at UCLA and four misses at Michigan).<ref name=AMlspbiMw>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/47870500/aday-mara-long-range-shooting-proves-big-michigan-win|title=Aday Mara's long-range shooting proves big in Michigan win|access-date=February 9, 2026|date=February 8, 2026|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/college-basketball/aday-mara-scores-24-points-no-2-michigan-routs-rival-ohio-state-82-61|title=Aday Mara Scores 24 Points as No. 2 Michigan Routs Rival Ohio State, 82-61|access-date=February 9, 2026|date=February 8, 2026|publisher=[[Fox Sports]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> Mara became the just the fourth NCAA Division I, {{convert|7|ft|3|in|m|1|adj=on}} player to make multiple three-point shots in a game since the [[2002–03 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2002–03 NCAA season]].<ref name=AMlspbiMw/>

Following the regular season, he was named Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year (the second in school history after [[Gary Grant (basketball)|Gary Grant]] in 1986 and 1987), as well as an All-Big Ten Defensive Team selection and an [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] third team selection by both the coaches and media.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2026/3/10/mens-basketball-lendeborg-earns-big-ten-player-of-the-year-as-u-m-hauls-15-all-conference-honors|title=Lendeborg Earns Big Ten Player of the Year as U-M and two blocks, as Michigan defeated [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], 91–73.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Garcia |first1=Tony |title=Michigan vanquishes Arizona, 91-73, in NCAA Final Four beatdown |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2026/04/04/michigan-arizona-final-four-game-score-yaxel-lendeborg/89469682007/ |access-date=April 5, 2026 |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=April 4, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aol.com/articles/heroes-zeros-michigan-final-four-045622050.html|website=[[AOL.com]]|first=Zach|last=Braziller|date=April 5, 2026|access-date=April 6, 2026|title=Heroes, zeros from Michigan's Final Four win over Arizona: Aday Mara was an absolute force}}</ref> On April 6, 2026, the team won the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|national championship]] and tied the [[Big Ten Conference]] record for single-season wins, 37.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2026/4/6/mens-basketball-wolverines-triumph-over-huskies-to-win-second-national-championship|title=Wolverines Triumph Over Huskies to Win Second National |website=[[ESPN.com]] |first=Jeff |last=Borzello |date=April 6, 2026 |access-date=April 7, 2026}}</ref> Mara was named to the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Final Four ==National team career==
Mara played for the [[Spain men's national under-17 basketball team|Spanish national team]] at the [[2022 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]] in Spain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/basketball/nba/2023/02/21/63f4bcb246163f56ad8b45c2.html|title=NBA grow excited about Spain's Aday Mara during the All-Star Weekend: The sky's the limit for him|first=Enrique|last=Corbella|work=[[Marca (newspaper)|MARCA]]|date=February 21, 2023|access-date=February 21, 2023}}</ref> He averaged 12.6 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 1.9 blocks per game, as Spain advanced to the final before losing to the United States.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.malagahoy.es/unicaja/TV-Espana-Francia-Mundo-FIBA-Malaga_0_1700230060.html|title=Cómo y dónde ver en TV el España-Francia de la Copa del Mundo FIBA sub 17 de Málaga|work=Málaga Hoy|date=July 9, 2022|access-date=February 21, 2023}}</ref> He was also on the Spanish national team for the [[2023 FIBA U18 European Championship]] in Serbia, again finishing as the runner-up and earning a silver medal.
